title: Trade, Energy and Regional Peace Dominate Abiy-Erdoğan Talks in Antalya
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan held bilateral talks in Antalya on 10 November on the sidelines of the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference, discussing ways to strengthen bilateral relations, particularly in trade and investment, alongside regional peace and issues of mutual interest.

title: Ethiopia, UK Discuss Climate Cooperation and COP32 Preparations
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Antalya, Türkiye -- Ethiopia and Britain discussed strengthening climate cooperation and preparations for next year's COP32 summit in Addis Ababa during talks on Thursday, Ethiopia's foreign ministry said.

title: Ethiopia's Green Energy Can Consolidate Competitive Edge in Textile, Garment Markets - German Deputy Ambassador
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's renewable energy resources could strengthen the competitiveness of its textile, garment, and leather products in European markets as international buyers increasingly consider sustainability alongside production standards, Germany's Deputy Ambassador in Ethiopia, Ferdinand von Weyhe said.

title: Forum Vows to Advocate Ethiopia's Strategic Interests in Nile, Red Sea
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The newly established Nile and Red Sea Strategic Forum pledged to strengthen research, policy advocacy, and public engagement to advance Ethiopia's strategic interests in the two vital waterways.

title: Ethiopia Steps Up Regional, Global Partnerships Ahead of COP32
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is stepping up diplomatic engagement with regional and international partners to strengthen climate cooperation and advance shared priorities ahead of hosting the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in 2027.

title: Algerian Delegates Hail Ethiopia's Dev't Model, Call for Stronger Pan-African Political Cooperation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Algeria's participation in the Second African Political Parties Summit 2026 has provided opportunity for the National Building Movement party to learn from Ethiopia's experience and exchange knowledge with political leaders and government officials, the Algerian party member Jarrallah Abdelmonem said.

title: News - Drought, Conflict Threaten Emergency-Level Food Insecurity in Tigray, Amhara, Afar
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Severe drought and escalating conflict are expected to push parts of Tigray, Amhara and Afar into Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels of food insecurity in early 2027, as widespread crop losses, disrupted markets and declining household purchasing power threaten to deepen an already deteriorating humanitarian situation, according to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET).

title: More Than 64, 000 Ethiopian Refugees, Asylum-Seekers Remain in War-Hit Sudan, UN Data Shows
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A total of 64,902 Ethiopian refugees and asylum-seekers were living in Sudan as of 31 October 2026, with more than two-thirds concentrated in Gedaref State, according to the latest figures released by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

title: From Boardrooms to Barracks: What Military Training for Senior Officials Signals Amid Rising Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- On 31 October 2026, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed joined ministers and other senior officials for military exercises at the Hurso training center. Photographs released by the prime minister's office showed civilian leaders taking part weeks after Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic ties. title: News - 'People Are Getting Desperate': Jimma Protests Expose Growing Anger Over Forced Conscription, Extortion
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Residents of Jimma city in southwestern Oromia zone in Ethiopia say protests that erupted on Monday and Tuesday were driven by mounting grievances over widespread forced conscription, arbitrary arrests, extortion and displacement, describing an increasingly desperate population with few avenues to seek redress from authorities.

title: Ethiopia Faces Contrasting Drought, Flood Risks As Potentially Record-Strength Super El Niño Looms
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia could face contrasting climate risks, with parts of the country exposed to worsening drought while southern areas brace for above-normal rainfall and potential flooding, as a potentially record-strength Super El Niño develops in 2026-27, according to an analysis by international water and sanitation organization WaterAid.

title: Ivorian Former Prime Minister Recognizes Ethiopia's Legitimate Sea Access Aspirations
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Former Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire and President of the Ivorian Popular Front (FPI), Pascal Affi N'Guessan, recognized Ethiopia's quest for sovereign sea access as a legitimate national aspiration.

title: COP32 Ethiopia Crucial Platform for Global South Consensus Beyond Climate Finance
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's hosting of COP32 in 2027 offers Global South nations a vital opportunity to build consensus, coordinate negotiating positions, and broaden climate discussions beyond financing, said Organization of Southern Cooperation (OSC) Secretary-General Manssour Bin Mussallam.

title: PM Abiy Urges Major Emitters to Step Up, Intensifies Diplomatic Outreach Ahead of Ethiopia's COP32
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed (PhD) has urged major greenhouse gas emitters to accelerate emissions reductions and deliver faster climate financing, as Ethiopia seeks to build international partnerships ahead of hosting the 32nd United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP32) in Addis Abeba next year.

title: Guterres Calls On Fossil Fuel Companies to Pay for Climate Damage
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called on governments to tax windfall profits of major fossil fuel companies and channel the proceeds into climate recovery efforts.

title: U.S. Banker Sees Strong Business Prospects, Significant Growth Potential in Ethiopia
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Chairman of the American Bankers Association (ABA) and Detroit-based First Independence Bank Chairman and CEO, Kenneth Kelly hailed Ethiopia's rising potential to attract foreign capital and financial sector transformation.

title: PM Abiy Says Ethiopia Taking Concrete Action to Address Climate Change
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has reaffirmed Ethiopia's commitment to tackling climate change through investments in renewable energy, large-scale tree-planting campaigns, climate-resilient agriculture, urban environmental protection, and electric mobility, stressing that climate action is an integral part of the country's economic policy.

title: PM Abiy Holds Talks With Qatar's Amir On Sidelines of COP31 Leaders' Summit
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed held a bilateral meeting with the Amir of the State of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al-Thani, on the sidelines of the COP31 Leaders' Summit.

title: Guterres Urges Climate Finance Equity for Developing Nations
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for an urgent increase in equitable climate financing for developing nations, warning that emerging economies outside China, representing nearly two-thirds of the global population, receive less than one-fifth of global clean energy investment.

title: As Conflict Spreads From Moyale to Borana, Cross Border, Domestic Livestock Markets Grind to a Halt
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A conflict that erupted in Moyale and spread to different parts of Borana, in southern Oromia, has entered its third week, severely disrupting daily life and bringing the areas main livestock market, a critical pillar of its economy, to a near standstill, residents told Addis Standard.

title: A Country Divided, a Region On Edge - Somalia Caught in the Crossfire of Foreign Rivalries
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Somalia is approaching a dangerous political and security crossroads. A confrontation over constitutional amendments, presidential tenure, and elections is increasingly intersecting with competition among foreign powers for influence across the Horn of Africa, the Gulf of Aden, and the Red Sea. title: U.S. Senators Send Second Letter to Rubio Urging Action to Avert Widening Conflict in Ethiopia
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A group of U.S. Democratic senators has sent a second letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging intensified American diplomatic intervention to prevent renewed fighting in Ethiopia and escalating tensions with Eritrea from developing into a wider regional conflict.

title: G7 Warns of Regional Escalation Risk As Ethiopia-Eritrea Tensions Worsen
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers have expressed concern over worsening tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea, warning that further escalation could destabilize the wider Horn of Africa and threaten regional security, humanitarian operations and international trade, including in the Red Sea.

title: Ethiopia Tells UN Envoy Eritrea, Sudan Backing Armed Groups and Drone Attacks
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has accused Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki and Sudan's army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan of supporting, arming and coordinating armed groups operating inside Ethiopia, including through repeated drone attacks, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's Horn of Africa adviser Getachew K. Reda said.

title: News - Renewed Fighting in Tigray Pushes Its Fragile Healthcare System Closer to Collapse, Again
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia has overwhelmed hospitals, disrupted medical services and deepened an already severe healthcare crisis in Tigray, with medical workers warning that civilians increasingly risk being left without access to emergency treatment, according to a report by National Public Radio (NPR).

title: Colours, Coffee And Hard Bargaining As Africa Makes Its Mark At COP31
summary: [Bird Story Agency] Africa has brought its colours, coffee and critical minerals to COP31. The last of those could be worth considerably more than all the diplomatic goodwill on offer in Antalya.

title: Ethiopia Committed to Collective Security, Says Major General Adamneh
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia remains committed to collective security with professionalism, discipline and sacrifice, Defense Peacekeeping Center Head Major General Adamneh Mengiste said.

title: Food Shortages Hit 71 Percent of Ethiopian Families Displaced Into Kenya's Moyale
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Tens of thousands of people who fled escalating conflict in Moyale along Ethiopia's border between Oromia and Somali regional states and crossed into northern Kenya are facing acute food shortages, inadequate shelter and limited access to clean water and healthcare, according to a new assessment by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and humanitarian partners.
